relation: Edge images of simple graphs and two list-decomposition conventions. An injective edge image ranges over the adjacent pairs of the pattern and need not lie in the host; an embedded copy also preserves adjacency. X47 decomposes by parts that are equal whenever they share an edge (repeated parts allowed); X212 counts every 2-element vertex set exactly as often as it is a host edge (repeated nonempty parts excluded, repeated empty parts allowed). Packing X47 writes its image with nested existentials over vertices, proved equal to the pair form; Cycle X212 uses the pair form verbatim. No tree, nonempty-pattern, connectedness or nonempty-part guard is added.
summary: Five source definitions (X47 copy and equal-part decomposition, X212 image, copy and exact-count decomposition), three complete rows (X47, X48, Barat-Thomassen) and the X47/X48 deepest Originals, which compose this family's raw copy with M1's raw edges, A11's raw minimum degree and the simple-cut family's raw cuts. The Barat-Thomassen row and the X212 definitions are unchanged since their creation and use no earlier migrated helper, so their frozen copies are their deepest originals. Earlier certificates are byte-preserved.

Atlas.foundations.tree_decompositions now imports no conjecture module: its seven declarations keep their names and are stated over E(G), GTBase.simple_cuts.cut_edges and GTBase.edge_copies. Six former types hold by conversion with their former bodies; x47_decomposition_x212's former premise used X47's nested-quantifier image, equal to the pair-form image only by proof, so its former contract is recovered through x47_tree_decomposition_by_copies_compat and x212_decomposition_into_copies_compat, not by conversion.
